claims.text: A data-driven synthesis approach guided by Bayesian optimization or deep learning can tune synthesis parameters to form noble-metal HEA three-dimensional nanoframeworks.
The proposed approach can produce atomic-level elemental mixing and controlled porosity.
Conventional processing of noble-metal HEA precursor mixtures yields disordered or poorly controlled nanoparticle aggregates.
Bayesian optimization or deep-learning models can iteratively adjust reaction parameters during synthesis to promote three-dimensional nanoframework formation.
Relevant adjustable parameters include temperature, heating rate, precursor concentration, and additive-manufacturing conditions.
High-temperature or in situ processing permits modulation of reaction kinetics.
Real-time feedback from in situ STEM can be used to update the synthesis model.
Uniform atomic mixing and controlled nucleation dynamics yield a porous three-dimensional framework with well-dispersed active sites.
Integrating experimental data and simulation outputs in a machine-learning framework enables rapid convergence on suitable synthesis conditions.
Machine-learning-selected synthesis conditions can balance elemental diffusion and reduce phase segregation.
Machine-learning-selected conditions promote self-assembly of a porous nanostructure with precise atomic control.
The resulting noble-metal HEA nanoframeworks will have greater surface area than conventionally synthesized materials.
The resulting nanoframeworks will exhibit a uniform distribution of active sites.
Greater surface area and uniformly distributed active sites will enhance catalytic performance relative to conventionally synthesized materials.
Conventional melting, rapid quenching, and traditional templating lack fine control over multielement mixing.
Conventional synthesis methods typically yield irregular or less-defined nanostructures.
The optimized conditions are sensitive to the quality and scope of the machine-learning training data.
Industrial scalability and reproducibility of the proposed approach remain unvalidated.
The magnitude of improvement in atomic ordering and catalytic activity remains uncertain pending systematic experimental comparisons.
The effectiveness of the proposed approach may vary with the particular noble-metal elements used.
